biological.citation: Abrogation of MAP4K4 protein function causes congenital anomalies in humans and zebrafish (PMID: 37126546)
biological.summary: Rare variants in MAP4K4 identified in 21 families with neurodevelopmental differences and multiple congenital anomalies were shown to be loss-of-function or dominant-negative alleles using zebrafish models. Decreasing Map4k4 activity in zebrafish caused developmental defects, and MAP4K4 was shown to negatively regulate RAS signaling in early embryonic stages. This establishes MAP4K4 as a causal locus for syndromic neurodevelopmental differences.

biological.citation: MAP4K4 negatively regulates CD8 T cell-mediated antitumor and antiviral immunity (PMID: 32220977)
biological.summary: Genetic deletion or pharmacologic inhibition of MAP4K4 enhances LFA-1 activation on CD8 T cells, improving their adherence to antigen-presenting cells and increasing T cell priming, proliferation, cytokine production, and cytotoxic activity. Loss of Map4k4 resulted in impaired tumor growth and improved antiviral responses in vivo, with ERM proteins (ezrin, radixin, moesin) identified as mediators between MAP4K4 and LFA-1. Inducible whole-body deletion of Map4k4 in adult mice was tolerated under homeostatic conditions.

biological.citation: RAP2 mediates mechanoresponses of the Hippo pathway (PMID: 30135582)
biological.summary: MAP4K4 (along with MAP4K6 and MAP4K7) was identified as a direct binding partner and downstream effector of the GTPase RAP2 in mechanotransduction. At low ECM stiffness, active RAP2 binds to and stimulates MAP4K4, resulting in activation of LATS1/2 and inhibition of YAP/TAZ, placing MAP4K4 in the Hippo signaling pathway as a mechanosensitive kinase. This defines a mechanosignaling pathway from ECM stiffness through RAP2-MAP4K4-LATS1/2 to the nucleus.

biological.citation: Cooperation of Striatin 3 and MAP4K4 promotes growth and tissue invasion (PMID: 35941177)
biological.summary: MAP4K4 was found to interact with striatin 3 and 4 (STRN3/4), with STRN3 coupling MAP4K4 to protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) to inactivate growth-repressing activities of MAP4K4. STRN3 also enables MAP4K4-mediated direct phosphorylation of VASP at S157 via its CNH domain interaction with striatins, which is necessary for efficient cell invasion in medulloblastoma. Depletion of either STRN3 or MAP4K4 reduces invasion, while loss of both abrogates tumor cell growth in cerebellar tissue.

biological.citation: MAP4K4 regulates forces at cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesions to promote collective cell migration (PMID: 37369604)
biological.summary: Using A431 carcinoma cells, MAP4K4 was identified as a central regulator of collective cell migration, with its inactivation blocking cluster migration and overexpression decreasing cluster cohesion. MAP4K4 promotes focal adhesion disassembly through phosphorylation of moesin and disassembles adherens junctions through a moesin-independent mechanism. Loss of MAP4K4 function leads to tensional disequilibrium in cell clusters, increasing traction forces and tension at cell-cell adhesions.

biological.citation: MAP4K4 exacerbates cardiac microvascular injury in diabetes by facilitating S-nitrosylation modification of Drp1 (PMID: 38724987)
biological.summary: MAP4K4 was found to be upregulated in diabetic cardiomyopathy and promotes S-nitrosylation of Drp1 (SNO-Drp1) at C644 in cardiac microvascular endothelial cells by inhibiting GPX4 expression, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and endothelial ferroptosis. Inhibition of MAP4K4 via DMX-5804 significantly reduced endothelial ferroptosis and alleviated cardiac microvascular dysfunction in db/db mice. A C650A mutation in mice abolished SNO-Drp1 and the associated cardiac microvascular disorder.

biological.citation: Histone lactylation-derived LINC01127 promotes the self-renewal of glioblastoma stem cells via the cis-regulating the MAP4K4 to activate JNK pathway (PMID: 38084701)
biological.summary: MAP4K4 expression in glioblastoma (GBM) is regulated in cis by the lncRNA LINC01127, which directly guides RNA polymerase II (POLR2A) to the MAP4K4 promoter region to upregulate its transcription. Elevated MAP4K4 expression activates the JNK signaling pathway, promoting self-renewal of GBM stem cells and phosphorylation of IκBα to sustain NF-κB activity. Targeting the LINC01127/MAP4K4/JNK/NF-κB axis impeded orthotopic tumor growth in GBM xenografts.

biological.citation: MAP4K4 aggravates microvascular anomalies in diabetic retinopathy in a YTHDF2-dependent manner (PMID: 40072537)
biological.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of fibrovascular membranes from proliferative diabetic retinopathy patients revealed MAP4K4 is predominantly expressed in retinal endothelial cells, with elevated expression compared to normal retinas. MAP4K4 expression and activity were upregulated in both PDR patient tissue and db/db mouse retinas, and its expression is post-transcriptionally regulated by the m6A reader YTHDF2, which modulates MAP4K4 mRNA stability. MAP4K4 promotes endothelial dysfunction and retinal microangiopathy through NF-κB signaling.

biological.citation: MAP4K4 promotes ovarian cancer metastasis through diminishing ADAM10-dependent N-cadherin cleavage (PMID: 36922678)
biological.summary: Transcriptomic sequencing of paired primary ovarian tumors and metastases revealed MAP4K4 is highly expressed at metastatic sites, with higher expression associated with poorer survival and more advanced disease stage. MAP4K4 stabilizes N-cadherin by mediating phosphorylation of ADAM10 at Ser436, suppressing ADAM10-dependent N-cadherin cleavage and promoting cancer cell adhesion, migration, and invasion. Pharmacologic inhibition of MAP4K4 abrogated peritoneal metastases in vivo.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Variants in MAP4K4 cause a novel and potentially treatable form of neurologic dysfunction with cardiac anomalies (Bhoj et al.)
biological.summary: Seven individuals from four families with variants in MAP4K4 (three truncating, one missense in a highly conserved region) presented with neurologic dysfunction and cardiac anomalies resembling a rasopathy, including Noonan-like syndrome features. MAP4K4 is noted to be extremely intolerant to missense variation (Z score 4.01) and has a maximum pLI score of 1, indicating strong constraint. The phenotype includes pulmonary artery stenosis, septal defects, and moderate-to-severe developmental delay.
